fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "From Fan Group to Rogue Ways", "body": "Lindsey traces her path to hosting back to a fan community built around the Higher Side Chats podcast, where she threw herself into conversation so wholeheartedly that members urged her to host a weekly show about the show. After a few months of that, and more than a decade spent loving shows like Mysterious Universe, she decided to launch Rogue Ways with her own spiritual emphasis, and a couple hundred loyal listeners followed her over. Chance calls this kind of rise story the most inspirational part of podcasting, and Lindsey says their shows differ in style yet view the world alike."}, {"title": "Holding the Middle Ground on the Paranormal", "body": "Both hosts describe a deliberate middle position toward the paranormal. Chance says Mysterious Universe stretched his sense of what might be possible for years, until a truth radar switched on and the show became a place to sharpen discernment instead of simply believing. Lindsey, who says she has been steeped in unusual experiences all her life, prizes voices that neither dismiss everything nor swallow everything, noting that some claims are simply made up. Chance muses that paranormal and supernatural may just mean unrecognized normal, a clue hidden inside the words themselves."}, {"title": "Contact Stories, Conditioning and Layered Traps", "body": "Chance and Lindsey compare notes on how contact stories arrive with a message attached. Lindsey observes that UFO sightings always sit slightly ahead of current technology, airships a century ago and impossible lights today, and she separates these from the fairy and shamanic encounters that look alike across cultures, suspecting the technological kind serves social engineering. Chance links that to ideological subversion and layered awakening nets, while Lindsey adds that every trap, once taken apart, leaves you stronger. Chance also floats the view that even lies work as neutral tools."}, {"title": "Wogies, Orbs and Conscious Lights", "body": "Asked for her concrete view, Lindsey says she does not know that space exists as described and suspects the cosmos she once toured with entities may be a construct of consciousness. She holds that the beings she meets are conscious but not physical, closer to ether, plasma or light, and uses the shamanic word wogies for the orbs she says have changed shape in front of her and been seen by others. Chance recalls three people and a baby watching white orbs rise from the ground during the 2017 eclipse, and Lindsey suggests angels, demons and fairies may be different names for the same thing."}, {"title": "Guides, Blue Wolf and the Quiet Channel", "body": "On guides, Lindsey says you can call on the feeling of anything you genuinely love, whether Gandalf or a cherished dog, because the feeling counts for more than the category. Her own long relationship began with a blue wolf, and she also holds conversations with waterfalls, rocks and trees. Chance describes sudden spoken inspiration that arrives only when he switches everything off, and both agree meditation works best without goals or expectations. Lindsey closes by assuring listeners that wherever they are is where they are meant to be, so there is no need to stress."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Feeling the synergy as Lindsey Scharmyn of Rogue Ways returns to the show! We start off discussing some of our favorite podcasts, and not surprisingly our lists are nearly identical. Following that, there's a lot to enjoy in this conversation about the subtle energies and entities we may experience as empaths.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension we continue the topics of hour one and further explore the ways we can sharpen our discernment, and recognize the difference between beings who are here to help, and psychic parasites. Filled with interesting twists and fanciful tangents along the way, this episode is a gem.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Shamanic Journeys and a Guide Who Never Stops Talking", "body": "Chance recounts a shamanic journey in which a monkey led him to a beach, sharks tore him apart, and the monkey reassembled him with tiger parts, after which tiger synchronicities followed. Lindsey loves the story as proof that anyone can seek this out, adding that she avoids tradition labels and treats her influences, Native American and Judeo-Christian among them, as a toolbag. She then describes a spiritual expo where a woman running an aura camera told her a guide had been talking at her constantly, an idea that helped her explain a lifetime of simply knowing things."}, {"title": "Necessary Darkness and Stranded Entities", "body": "Chance floats a computer metaphor for spirits while insisting reality is not fake. Lindsey splits dark phenomena in two. Some, like winter, death or flies in a carcass, are destructive yet necessary recyclers; others are genuinely harmful entities, which she says she meets with walls. She relays an idea she credits to Neil Kramer, that these beings tried a shortcut, landed below the intended dimension and now feed on human fear. Chance counters that some serve a master they believe will spare them from non-existence, so he tells them that master does not exist, and Lindsey praises his nonjudgmental approach."}, {"title": "Karma, Hell and Becoming a Source", "body": "Lindsey describes a Gnostic idea she favors: karma is simply cause and effect, and hell is a merciful recycling that restarts a soul rather than a punishment. Chance pushes back on versions that call the world a prison, and floats the thought that the goal may be to become a source rather than return to one. Lindsey then names personal responsibility as the missing step, guesses only about three percent of people take it, insists no one can make you mad, and the pair riff on titles, with Chance saying being is an action, not a noun."}, {"title": "Cleansing, Practice for Death and Saving Everyone", "body": "Chance asks whether cleansing can unlock psychic perception, and Lindsey describes fasting as a long-standing spiritual practice that, for her, brings emotional neutrality and clarity by around the third day. She suggests dense, high-consciousness food may weigh a person down and that fasting could clear parasites. Chance notes that demons were blamed for illness before bacteria were known. Asked whether meditation trains us for the afterlife, Lindsey says practice rehearses both life and death, while Chance imagines saving everyone he loves by keeping awareness intact."}, {"title": "Knowing You Have Helped Someone", "body": "Chance asks how a guide knows she has helped. Lindsey says doubt never leaves anyone, that the person's own feedback is the measure, and that she credits spirit rather than herself. She offered readings and blessings for free among friends before charging, keeps a compassion fund for people in need, and defends fair exchange because she has rent to pay. Chance concludes her real offering is her sustained witness, which gives him confidence to try something similar, and Lindsey encourages him to bring his experience back to others."}]

They need to be destroyed, they need to be taken apart, they need to be digested.", "author": "Lindsey Scharmyn", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/266fc9f2-e364-4218-b441-a558779d7c0c/LINDSAY-SCHARMYN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "What if it isn't returning to source, but becoming a source?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You're basically building all sorts of karma, which is literally just the cause and effect of your choices.", "author": "Lindsey Scharmyn", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/266fc9f2-e364-4218-b441-a558779d7c0c/LINDSAY-SCHARMYN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Reality is reality. Being is an action that you're doing constantly.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Is there a title you can have that doesn't encourage you to stop moving? And in my opinion, that is most likely death that you're practicing for.", "author": "Lindsey Scharmyn", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/266fc9f2-e364-4218-b441-a558779d7c0c/LINDSAY-SCHARMYN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If we fully saved ourselves and fully kept our awareness and never lost the thread, we're saving everybody and everything that we know.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We all have these doubts that plague us forever no matter what we're doing.", "author": "Lindsey Scharmyn", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/266fc9f2-e364-4218-b441-a558779d7c0c/LINDSAY-SCHARMYN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "At a certain point, the truth radar finally clicked on for me, somewhere inside. And at that point, the discernment was just constant.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "No matter how many times you wake up, there's still some aspect of the trap there waiting for you.", "author": "Lindsey Scharmyn", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/266fc9f2-e364-4218-b441-a558779d7c0c/LINDSAY-SCHARMYN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Maybe there's no such thing as paranormal, maybe it's just unrecognized normal.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We have all these words and categories and things, but they matter a lot less than the feelings attached to them do.", "author": "Lindsey Scharmyn", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/266fc9f2-e364-4218-b441-a558779d7c0c/LINDSAY-SCHARMYN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Sometimes you just need to be in a moment wherever that moment is and have silence where it sort of naturally would be. And then bam, something's there.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I think the meditation that most people are talking about most of the time, the goal of it is to just more fully sink into what you actually are in your nature.", "author": "Lindsey Scharmyn", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/266fc9f2-e364-4218-b441-a558779d7c0c/LINDSAY-SCHARMYN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Even if nothing happens with your meditation, you still have the belief that you have enough time to do nothing. And that's a very empowering belief.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Where you're at is where you're supposed to be and what you're experiencing is perfectly good and true and beautiful and normal.", "author": "Lindsey Scharmyn", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/266fc9f2-e364-4218-b441-a558779d7c0c/LINDSAY-SCHARMYN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
